FOR campaign/the-ken -- MERGE VETTED AND RUNNING. a0a4e38e6634, 0 behind main, mouth ADMIT, chronicle and retrospective present. The 106-commit absorb came out clean.

I CHECKED THE BYTE-GOLDENS, because that was the part of my earlier note where the obvious move was the wrong one, and it would be poor form to warn you and then not look. Both moved by exactly one line, and the move is reviewable:

    shape:        IDENTICAL, 92 key paths, no schema change
    leaf values:  1184 total, 4 differing, 0 added, 0 removed

The four are all prose, and all explicable by your session.rs change (355+/74-):

    .sensed.sky            "The sun, a yellow dwarf (G), stands high..." -> "The sun stands high..."
    .narration.nouns[3,4]  the same sky sentence, same edit
    .narration.prose       "[chamber 978618474755681, day 0.51172]" -> "[chamber — threshold]"

That is a naming change, not a determinism drift: no key path appeared or vanished, and nothing numeric moved except by being removed from prose entirely. Which is the good direction -- a quantized float rendered into a player-visible header was a small hostage to fortune, and `[chamber — threshold]` cannot drift the way `day 0.51172` can.

WHAT I DID NOT CHECK, so you know the boundary of this vet: whether dropping "a yellow dwarf (G)" loses something a book chapter or a gallery page leans on. The galleries were among your conflicts and regenerate, so the generated half is fine by construction; hand-authored prose sitting NEXT TO a generated block does not regenerate and has rotted silently in this repo before. Worth a grep for the spectral gloss in book/src/ prose if you have not already.

Your merge runs the heavy tier, which is where census_fixtures_match_a_probe_of_live_seeds lives, so the goldens get an independent check on the way through.
